source: Reviewed summary of an automated fixture-v2 run launched from WSL through Windows Node and headless Windows Chrome. The full generated report remains in the ignored model-evaluation-results directory because it contains raw model responses.

environment.note: The runtime model confirms shader-f16 availability. No GPU adapter details were captured.

reviewedAllCases.method: The thirteen accepted cases use app scores. The two completed rejected responses were reviewed using the established occurrence-level method: exact duplicate literal/category pairs are deduplicated, returned literals are expanded to their source occurrences, unmatched or conflicting detections count as extras, and only exact expected span/category pairs count as correct.

endToEndOutput.method: Rejected documents produce no partial output. Their four expected occurrences therefore count as missed, while their rejected raw detections do not count as output replacements.

timing.note: Timing includes all fifteen completed generations, including the two responses rejected by validation.

validationFailureReview.name: ID and account distinction
validationFailureReview.error: One returned person name did not occur in the source.

validationFailureReview.name: Name parts with ordinary meanings
validationFailureReview.error: The response assigned conflicting categories to the repeated literals May and Chen.

notableAcceptedCases: Contact details found all four expected occurrences but added two extras.
Address and date of birth was the only perfect original v1 case in this run.
The first clean-negative case produced thirteen extra replacements; the second produced one.
Unicode contact details was perfect, while the international phone case had no correct exact span/category matches.
The non-Latin name and email were both found, with one extra replacement.
conclusion: The 0.6B WebLLM path completed all fifteen generations but remained unreliable. End-to-end output replaced 17/30 expected occurrences and added 28 incorrect replacements. The expanded negative cases confirm that over-redaction is not confined to a single fixture.
